title: Momentum and kinetic energy
hook: Change momentum magnitude and predict kinetic energy.
misconception: kinetic energy doubles when momentum magnitude doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply K = p²/(2m) to compare kinetic energy when momentum magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a nonrelativistic particle of fixed mass, K = p²/(2m). When momentum magnitude doubles, kinetic energy becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model K = p²/(2m); scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a nonrelativistic particle of fixed mass, with a nonzero initial result. If momentum magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on kinetic energy?
recall.why: Apply K = p²/(2m) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
